thread:
maria: Quick flag  onboarding Astra-11B int8. baseline fp16 vs int8 eval on long-context summarization shows weird periodic hallucinations and repeated phrase echoes after ~1k tokens. suspect rotary phasewrap + tokenizer unicode normalization mismatch.

dan: Can you drop the tiny repro and perf numbers?

maria: command used:
```
./tools/run_eval.sh --model astra-11b --dtype int8 --prompts longdoc_5000.txt --max-tokens 2048 --seed 42 --batch 2
```
metrics (fp16 -> int8):
- RougeL: 45.6 -> 40.2
- EM: 82.1 -> 74.0
- p95 latency: 310ms -> 110ms
- failure pattern: repeated 3-token echo every ~256 tokens, and occasional token id <unk> insertion near quotes.

oliver: Did you use the hf tokenizer import that applies NFKC? we had one model where NFKC changed composed characters and shifted token boundaries causing rotary index misalignment.

maria: I used tokenizer_import.py v2 which does NFKC by default. Dump of token sequences around the quote boundary shows different token lengths between converters: 
```
# fp16 token ids around pos 1021..1034: [987, 988, 1023, 1024, 1027] (len 14 tokens for phrase)
# int8 token ids (converted via v2 nfkc): [987, 988, 1024, 1025, 1028] (len 13 tokens)
```
looks like a merge/split around soft-hyphen + non-breaking space.

dan: That could cause the rotary lookup (which uses token position->cos/sin tables) to be off by one for subsequent tokens, generating a phase shift that accumulates and eventually wraps. Have you pulled the runtimes rotary metadata?

maria: runtime dump: 
```
rotary: {base: 10000, head_dim: 64, per_head_scale: false, freq_method: "legacy"}
int8-kernel: autotuned to freq_scale=0.985 (runtime override)
per-head adjustments: none
```

oliver: If freq_scale != 1 and tokenizer changes tokenization lengths, you can see phase misalignment at boundaries. Also int8 kernels may quantize rotary tables differently; the low-bit interpolation can introduce periodic error that looks like echoing.

dan: Proposed quick checks:
1) run tokenmap-diff between nfkc-on vs nfkc-off for 100 canonical sentences.
2) force int8 freq_scale=1.0 and re-eval to isolate quant kernel effect.
3) produce per-head cos/sin L2 diff between fp16 tables and int8 tables after quantization.

maria: did 2) first: forcing freq_scale=1.0 reduced echo amplitude but didn't remove it (RougeL 42.8). Suggests mixed cause.

maria: ran tokenmap-diff on canonical set: found 17/100 sentences with changed token counts; many involve soft hyphen (\u00AD) and narrow no-break space (\u202F).

dan: OK. next: try converting tokenizer with NFKC disabled and preserve original composed glyphs; see if sequence lengths align. Also run a short per-head rotary recalibration on a 10k-token corpus to re-derive quantized cos/sin tables.

oliver: I pushed a small tool change that flags any tokenization length delta >1 in CI: PR-4599. We should gate new tokenizers.

maria: did a quick run using nfkc disabled + freq_scale=1.0 + per-head requantize (5k steps). Results: RougeL 44.9, EM 80.3. Much closer. No obvious periodic echo in the sample set.

dan: Good sign. Action items:
- maria: open PR with tokenizer conversion notes and add canonical-sentences check (you already have PR-4599 but include astra case).
- oliver: add runtime flag to lock rotary_freq_scale and a CI job that compares quantized rotary tables to fp16 baseline within tolerance.
- ops-bot: schedule a canary int8 deploy for Astra on dedicated pool once PRs land.

ops-bot: deploy:quant-kernels/2026-03-23 09:12 UTC -> Canary queued (4 gpus) pending PR merge.

maria: I'll upload annotated failing prompts + logits diffs to /shared/onboard/astra/phasewrap/ and start a 1k blind AB against fp16.

dan: If AB still shows small gaps, consider per-head calibration with stratified long/short buckets. That tends to fix headwise interpolation artifacts.

oliver: Also add a short note in onboarding checklist: "avoid NFKC by default; verify token counts across HF versions".

maria: Done. Thanks team. Will follow up with AB results in this thread.
